name: Antipodal Pairs Do Not Certify a Safe Convex Restriction
statement: For every $d\ge4$ there is a learning space $\mathcal P_d$ of isometric dimension $d+1$ whose positive semicube in a coordinate $e$ induces a nonlearning partial cube $\mathcal F_d$ of isometric dimension $d$, even though $\mathcal F_d$ contains the antipodal pairs $\{i\},X\setminus\{i\}$ for every $i\ne a$. Thus antipodality alone does not make a convex restriction of a learning-space graph safe.
proof: The restriction $\mathcal F_d$ is a translate of $\mathcal T_d$, so it is well graded, union closed in its displayed orientation, and has no valid root. Adding the empty state produces a union-closed well-graded family $\mathcal B_d$. Stacking $\mathcal B_d$ below a positive $e$-fiber equal to $\mathcal F_d$ gives the union-closed well-graded parent $\mathcal P_d$. The stated complementary pairs avoid all deleted states of $\mathcal F_d$.
